points.t: Central facial redness, flushing, papules or pustules, **no comedones**; triggered by heat, alcohol, spice.
Neurovascular hyper-reactivity + innate immunity (cathelicidin, TLR2); *Demodex* amplifies.
Triggers, daily SPF, gentle skincare; ivermectin for papules, brimonidine for redness, doxycycline 40 mg MR if moderate–severe.
**Eye pain, photophobia, reduced vision** (same-day). Flushing with diarrhoea or wheeze.

cause.lead: Reactive vessels, reactive immunity, too many mites.
points: **Heat, spicy food, hot drinks** activate TRPV1 → neuropeptides → vasodilation.
**Alcohol** (red wine), **UV** (cathelicidin via kallikrein-5), cold, wind, exercise, stress, menopause.
**Demodex**: 6–15× more mites; they activate TLR2. Teach “contributor and amplifier”.
**Topical steroids / TCIs**: vasodilation, mite overgrowth, rebound on stopping.
Flushing drugs: nicotinic acid, CCBs, nitrates, sildenafil, opioids, tamoxifen.

visuals.caption: Rosacea skin: widened vessels just under the surface (telangiectasia), inflamed papules and a pustule, and Demodex mites crowding a follicle. Note: no comedone plug.

features.lead: Name each phenotype; treat each one.
points: **Diagnostic** (one is enough): persistent centrofacial erythema, or **phyma**.
**Major**: flushing, papules / pustules, telangiectasia, **ocular** signs.
**Minor**: burning, stinging, oedema, dryness.
**Skin of colour**: redness subtle or brownish; look for papules, warmth, stinging history.
Record **phenotype + severity + QoL** at every review.

visuals.caption: Where rosacea sits: the convex central face (cheeks, nose, chin, central forehead), with the skin around the eyes spared and no comedones.
visuals.alt: Face showing central facial distribution of rosacea

items.name: Papulopustular
items.t: Dome-shaped papules and pustules, no comedones.

items.name: Phymatous
items.t: Thickened skin, contour change; mostly men.

items.name: Steroid rosacea
items.t: Fiery red, burning; flares within days of stopping.

points: Diagnosis is clinical.
Comedones dominate? **Rethink acne**.
Diarrhoea, wheeze, palpitations: **5-HIAA**, tryptase.
Headache, sweats, hypertension: metanephrines.
Every cream, strength and duration, incl. OTC, online, **skin-lightening**.
Dermoscopy: ‘Demodex tails’.
Scaly and asymmetric? Scrape for **tinea incognito**.

cards.name: Perioral dermatitis
cards.clue: Perioral papules, vermilion border spared; after steroids.

cards.name: Seborrhoeic dermatitis
cards.clue: Greasy scale in nasolabial folds, brows; often coexists.

manage.lead: Phenotype-based (NICE CKS). Confirm doses in the BNF.

points: Trigger diary; gentle, fragrance-free skincare.
**Daily SPF** (mineral if sensitive).
**Stop facial steroids / TCIs.**

rx.dur: Up to 4 months; repeat courses allowed
rx.note: CKS first line; anti-Demodex. Transient burning.
Rebound / paradoxical erythema in ~10–20%: test a small area. Not for flushing.
Licensed. Not in pregnancy or under 12. Erythromycin if tetracyclines unsuitable.

points: Low-dose isotretinoin (PPP applies) for refractory disease or phyma.
Laser / IPL for telangiectasia (usually private).
Steroid rosacea: taper, warn of a 1–3-week rebound, cover with an oral tetracycline.

limits.t: Never without a specialist plan. OTC hydrocortisone licence excludes the face.
Maintenance topical therapy is often needed.

items.t: **Eye pain, photophobia or reduced vision**: possible keratitis → ophthalmology.
Flushing with **diarrhoea, wheeze, palpitations or hypotension**: carcinoid or mastocytosis.
Photosensitive malar rash with systemic symptoms: exclude **lupus**.
Rash after potent topical steroids: stop or taper with support; refer if severe.

pearls.t: **No comedones + flushing + central face = rosacea** until proven otherwise.
Fails metronidazole or azelaic acid, scaly or itchy? Think **Demodex** → ivermectin.
Mites are on everyone: not a hygiene problem.
Ask about skin-lightening creams kindly: clobetasol and mercury products are illegal in the UK.

quiz.q: Which lesion is absent in rosacea but the hallmark of acne?

quiz.a: Ivermectin 1% cream once daily, up to 4 months.

quiz.q: What is the key warning with brimonidine gel?
quiz.a: Rebound or paradoxical erythema in about 10–20%: test a small area first. It is for persistent redness, not flushing.

quiz.q: Licensed oral option for moderate–severe rosacea?
quiz.a: Doxycycline 40 mg MR once daily for 16 weeks, then review.
